localChanges: chore: lock the engine packages that let computer players bargain, threaten and keep their word

log: The ruleset's judgement of how many defenders a city builds up to and how many it keeps fortified and calls idle units in to (civ-clone/web-renderer#423).

The computer player's stance (MeetWithKing.cs F6_0000_0000 steps 1-9: fear, tribute, hostility, peace desire, its Senate, sham peace) decides a one-path negotiation map: knowledge, cancel-treaty, tribute in gold or an advance, then war (provoked/rejected/first contact) or peace, sweetened when refused (advance, gold, everything) and war if still refused; at peace it hands over and pays what it fears to refuse. Two computer players settle it with F0_2517_0b1d. Resolved rules move the tribute and gifts, declare war, sign peace and record grudges; a sham peace is dropped silently one turn in three; a nuclear strike earns a Vendetta; MayNegotiate rules give the 16/32- and 4-turn intervals. civ-clone/web-renderer#427, #71.
v474.05 calls F0_2517_0cef at every peaceful meeting, treaty or not; only signing the treaty was conditional.
Initial commit: v474.05's ranking score and military strength as core-power rules
A generic measure of how strong a player is, made of rules a ruleset fills in (civ-clone/web-renderer#71, #149's rank half).

Directional declarations for a grudge and a peace kept only for now, a call to cancel a third party's treaty, a sweetened peace offer, DemandTribute#kind, and a MayNegotiate rule (with mayNegotiate's 15-turn fallback) so a ruleset says how often players talk. civ-clone/web-renderer#427.

Computer players no longer break a peace on the map whenever their raw attack+defence matches the other's (shouldAttack and shouldBeHostile are removed): a treaty ends only by a war declared in a meeting or a dropped sham peace (civ1-diplomacy). chooseNegotiationStep accepts where it may choose, otherwise takes the one step offered. civ-clone/web-renderer#427.
